page: Microsoft Azure B2ps_v2 is a burstable virtual machine belonging to the Bpsv2 server family, built on the arm64 architecture. It features 2 vCPUs powered by an Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. This configuration provides 2 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, backed by 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable, allowing connection to external high-performance storage volumes.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the B2ps_v2 delivers modest performance, aligning with its burstable design. In single-core stress-ng testing, the server achieves an average score of 1822.08, while its multi-core score drops to a weak 3597.88. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 140.71 GB/sec, but uncached large block read and write speeds fall to 26.73 GB/sec and 16.97 GB/sec respectively. Single-threaded gzip compression performs at an average rate of 24.19 GB/sec, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is poor at 16.71 GB/sec. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 1112.0 and a multi-core score of 2025.0, reflecting its entry-level computational capabilities.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the B2ps_v2 offers a highly economical resource profile for workloads that do not require continuous full CPU utilization. The burstable CPU allocation model allows users to pay for baseline performance while retaining the ability to handle occasional spikes. However, the tradeoffs include poor performance in intensive tasks such as LLM inference, where a small 135M model achieves only 89.05 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 37.26 tokens/sec for text generation. This server is best suited for low-traffic web serving, lightweight database operations, development environments, and basic background tasks.
